mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 3.5%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 3.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5pp in 3 months) signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a robust labor market that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline does not produce positive 60-day returns in > 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized) signals sustained economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive during late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized) compared to other regimes (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) indicates weakening economic supply capacity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline does not predict negative 5-day returns (Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in housing starts (HOUST > 10% YoY) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 10% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE < 3.5%), rising wage pressures fuel inflation, prompting central bank tightening that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the effect is not observed in the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0%) and elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) signal a restrictive monetary environment that suppresses corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 6.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% does not produce negative 5-day returns in > 60% of cases (t-test p>0.05).
